question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> different wavelength may be observed in the spectrum from a hydrogen sample if the atoms are excited to states with principal quantum number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>? The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Use the concept of hydrogen like atom spectrum when the atoms are excited to a sixth excited state, to find different wavelengths observed in the spectrum.

The total possible transitions are,

 nn-12=6×52=15

Here n is the principal quantum number.
